question: Who will win the 2026 U.S. Senate election in New Hampshire — Democrat Chris Pappas or Republican John Sununu?
title: New Hampshire U.S. Senate — Pappas vs. Sununu
resolution: Resolves to the winner of the New Hampshire U.S. Senate general election on Nov 3, 2026, following the Sept 8, 2026 primaries.

consensus.headline_case: Pappas is favored for the open seat Jeanne Shaheen is vacating, but the case is a lean, not a lock. The exact-question market prices him near 84-85 cents, backed by a roughly 2:1 cash-on-hand edge ($5.2M to $2.7M after Q2) and a Trump approval collapse in the state (37/62, net -25, the worst since October 2017). But live general-election polling shows a single-digit and tightening race — Pappas led Sununu 49-42 in April, 47-44 by late June, and Emerson had them flatly tied in March — which argues the raw market price overstates the current state of play. Marking the price down for that compression, and for the fact this is an open seat rather than an incumbent defense, lands a 70-78% modal band for a Pappas win.
consensus.why_over_runner_up: Sununu is deliberately priced well above the market's implied 15-16%, because he is a materially stronger candidate than the Republicans who lost this seat badly in 2020 and 2022 — a former two-term U.S. Senator with statewide name ID, not a first-time nominee. New Hampshire also just proved it will split its ticket at scale: it backed Harris by only 2.8 points in 2024 (down from Biden's 7.3-point win in 2020) while electing Republican Kelly Ayotte governor by 9.3 points the same day. Sununu stays the runner-up because the environment — an unpopular Republican president, a cash-starved campaign, and a Democratic nominee with five terms of statewide-adjacent vote-getting — outweighs candidate quality on its own.
consensus.dissent: The Contrarian's case: the 84-85 cent market is pricing in the 2020/2022 pattern (weak GOP nominees losing by 9-16 points) onto a race that doesn't match it. This is the one Republican-leaning open seat comp NH has produced since 2010 — and in that case (Ayotte over Hodes) the Republican won by 16. A tightening trend that ran the Pappas lead from +7 to +3 in ten weeks, if it continues past Labor Day, plausibly reaches a toss-up by November. Read that way Sununu belongs in the low-to-mid 30s, not the high teens.

profiles.name: The Market Reader
profiles.criterion: Sides with the price the sharpest, deepest, most liquid markets have settled on.
profiles.blurb: Polymarket's exact-question contract prints Democrat at 85 cents, Republican at 17. I'd normally just take that number, but total volume here is $38k - thin next to a race this nationally watched, and Kalshi lists the same contract without a price I could confirm at pull time. A tape this thin can run ahead of the news. I dock it five or six points for liquidity risk and land at 80, favored but not blowout-favored.

profiles.name: The Quant
profiles.criterion: Trusts the simulation models and structured decompositions over recency and sentiment.
profiles.blurb: Break it into stages. P(Pappas wins the Dem primary) is ~0.97 off a 53-29 lead over Manzur. Conditional on the general-election matchup, P(Sununu is the GOP nominee) is ~0.85 given his 48-19-to-59-20 primary leads and the Trump endorsement; P(Brown nominee) ~0.12. Pappas's polling edge is +3 against Sununu (47-44) but +9 against Brown (48-39), so weight those: 0.85(0.80) + 0.12(0.85) + 0.03(0.75) is about 0.80, times the 0.97 primary factor is about 0.78. I round down slightly for the tightening trend the polling itself shows.
profiles.evidence: Dem primary 53-29 Pappas over Manzur; GOP primary Sununu 48-59% vs Brown; general matchup Pappas-Sununu 47-44, Pappas-Brown 48-39.

profiles.name: The Historian
profiles.criterion: Counted reference-class base rates and venue history.
profiles.blurb: I count what New Hampshire has actually done, not what it's said it will do. Three of the last four top-of-ballot Senate contests went Democratic - but the fourth, the only true open seat in that set, went Republican by sixteen points when Ayotte beat Hodes in 2010. This is that same shape again: no incumbent, a credible GOP nominee, a midterm. And the ledger keeps writing itself past that one race - Harris carried this state by only 2.8 in 2024, less than half of Biden's 7.3, the same day the voters sent a Republican to the governor's chair by 9.3. The venue is drifting redder than the market wants to admit.
profiles.evidence: NH top-of-ballot Senate since 2010: 3 D wins (2016 +0.14, 2020 +15.6, 2022 +9.1) vs. 1 R win (2010 open seat, +16); 2024 Harris +2.8 (down from Biden +7.3 in 2020) vs. Ayotte (R) governor +9.3 same ballot.

profiles.name: The Path Reader
profiles.criterion: Ignores reputation; reads the actual route, mechanism, and path dependence.
profiles.blurb: Follow the mechanism. Pappas has won NH-1, a genuine swing district, five straight times - he already knows how to build a statewide-adjacent coalition. He carries a 2:1 cash edge into the fall and a Trump approval crater (net -25) that depresses GOP-leaning turnout and energizes his own base. Sununu's route runs through ticket-splitters who backed Ayotte for governor, and those voters exist - but they have to show up twice, once at the top for Sununu against a well-funded, well-known challenger. That's a heavier lift than the coattail-free governor's race Ayotte won. Route favors Pappas, closely.
profiles.evidence: Pappas cash-on-hand $5.2M vs. Sununu $2.7M; Trump NH net approval -25 (37/62); Pappas's five-term NH-1 win streak in a competitive district.

profiles.name: The Talisman
profiles.criterion: Elite individual actors, motivation, proven leadership.
profiles.blurb: I read the man, not the tape. Here is a five-term Congressman who has never lost a race in a district Republicans should win, running now for an open seat his own mentor is vacating. Against him: a comeback candidate, seventeen years removed from the Senate, who called Trump 'a loser' in print before turning around to accept his endorsement - a man running as someone he wasn't a decade ago. Voters can smell that seam. Pappas's is the steadier hand, and steadier hands win open seats in states this exhausted with Washington drama.
profiles.evidence: Pappas undefeated across five NH-1 cycles; Sununu's 17-year absence from elected office and his prior public 'Trump is a loser' op-ed preceding the Trump endorsement.

profiles.name: The Contrarian
profiles.criterion: Favorites usually fail; hunts the underpriced live path.
profiles.blurb: Everyone's piled onto the 85-cent side, which is exactly where I go looking. The polling trend nobody's pricing: Pappas led by 7 in April, by 3 in late June, and Emerson had it a flat tie back in March - that's not a stable lead, that's a lead in motion, and it's moving the wrong way for the favorite. Sununu is also simply a better candidate than the two men who got blown out here in 2020 and 2022, and Ayotte just showed a real GOP floor in this state nine months ago. I'll take Sununu in the low-to-mid thirties and let the September post-primary polls come to me.
profiles.evidence: Pappas-Sununu margin compressed from +7 (April) to +3 (June); Emerson tie in March; Ayotte (R) governor win by 9.3 points in 2024.

profiles.name: The Prophet
profiles.criterion: Divine providence; backs the fated, story-shaped outcome the ending events seem to be scripting.
profiles.blurb: Watch the timing. Trump's approval in this state hits its lowest mark since October 2017 in the very month the general election clock starts running - a coincidence too neat to be one. And watch the man on the other side: Sununu returns to a stage he left in 2009, endorsed by a president he once called a loser, in a state that has spent a decade rewarding candidates who stay who they are. Pappas never had to reinvent himself. The story that keeps its own promises is the one where the steady man wins the seat the storm-tossed one is chasing back.
profiles.evidence: Trump NH approval hits lowest point since Oct 2017 (net -25) in the opening month of the general; Sununu's return bid follows a public reversal on his past Trump criticism.

base_rates.text: NH top-of-ballot U.S. Senate races since 2010 went Democratic (2016 Hassan +0.14, 2020 Shaheen +15.6, 2022 Hassan +9.1); the exception, 2010's Ayotte-Hodes race, is also the only other true open seat in the set - and it went Republican by 16.

triggers: The September 8, 2026 primary results themselves - a Brown upset of Sununu, or a Manzur upset of Pappas, would reset every downstream number.
Two consecutive post-Labor-Day likely-voter polls showing the Pappas-Sununu gap inside 2 points, or Sununu ahead - would validate the Contrarian and Historian and shift mass toward Sununu.
Two consecutive polls showing Pappas back above a 6-7 point lead - would reverse the spring-to-summer tightening trend and shift mass toward a comfortable Pappas win.
A further drop in Trump's NH approval below net -30, or a rebound above net -20 - the single largest environmental lever on both campaigns' turnout math.
Q3 FEC filings (due mid-October) showing Sununu closing the cash gap below 1.5:1 via national GOP transfers, or Pappas's lead widening past 3:1.
A Polymarket/Kalshi re-pricing with materially higher volume than the current thin ~$38k - would upgrade the market from a soft signal to a strong anchor.

A specific ticket-splitting signal in the crosstabs - e.g., a poll showing Ayotte-2024 voters breaking for Sununu at a rate near the governor's race margin - would sharpen the Path Reader's and Historian's read.
A candidate-defining event (health issue, scandal, high-profile gaffe, or a major third-party endorsement) for either nominee.

method_note: Anchored on Polymarket's exact-question market (Democrat 84-85%, thin volume of ~$38k, pulled Aug 1 2026); Kalshi lists the same contract but no confirmed live price could be pulled at request time. The raw market price is marked down because live general-election polling shows a single-digit and tightening race (UNH: Pappas 47-Sununu 44 in June, down from Pappas 49-42 in April; Emerson: a flat 45-44 tie in March) and because New Hampshire ticket-split sharply in 2024 (Harris +2.8, down from Biden +7.3, on the same ballot that elected Republican Kelly Ayotte governor by 9.3). Both primaries (Pappas over Manzur; Sununu, Trump-endorsed, over Brown) are treated as near-certain outcomes of the Sept 8, 2026 vote given commanding polling leads on both sides. Horizon: through November 3, 2026.
honesty_note: The market's 84-85% reads as structurally overconfident once the actual polling trend is priced in - Pappas's lead has been shrinking, not holding, for three straight polling waves. Treat 70-78% as a real lean with a genuinely live Republican path, not a settled outcome. Sununu is a far more credible statewide candidate than the nominees Shaheen and Hassan beat by 9-16 points in 2020 and 2022, and this cycle's shape - an open seat, a swing state that just elected a Republican governor by 9 points, a comeback candidate with real name ID - most resembles 2010, the one recent case in this reference class where New Hampshire flipped.
